clue.text: Attempts to keep posh island gardens in Paris

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it inside, so these words put the next pieces within the first

parts.note: tries are attempts
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage
ile is French for island, apt for a Paris clue

explanation.surface: Someone tries to keep a smart island garden going somewhere in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: ILE is the French for island, fitting the Paris setting; the gardens are the formal park beside the Louvre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jardin des Tuileries is the celebrated public park in central Paris, near the Louvre.

clue.text: Waterworks' official ensures ships' company has food to go round

indicators.note: food going round the other pieces means it encloses them

parts.note: tuck is British slang for food, especially snacks
RN, the Royal Navy, owns the nation's warships

explanation.surface: A waterworks officer makes sure the crew have enough food to share round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensures' and 'has' only join the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncock was the waterworks employee who turned the street mains on and off.

clue.text: Part of 14 and of elevated newspapers

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised or elevated means the letters are read from the bottom up
this second of repeats the earlier part of, so only a portion of the word is taken

parts.note: dailies are daily newspapers

explanation.surface: Something forms part of a longer work and also of some upmarket papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' does double service: the Iliad is part of Homer's work (14 is CHAPMAN'S HOMER), and part of DAILIES (DAILI, ES dropped), turned up by 'elevated', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's two epics are the Iliad and the Odyssey, so this poem is one portion of his output.

clue.text: No problem with arrival or departure

definitions.text: No problem with arrival or departure

parts.words: No problem with arrival or departure
parts.note: read as something arriving without trouble and leaving without trouble, the idiom for things gained and lost lightly

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an attitude where gains and losses are taken casually, as neither coming nor going matters.

clue.text: Essential hormone found in rising of Latin river

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read upwards, reversing the letters

parts.note: Nilus is the Latin name for the river Nile

explanation.surface: A vital hormone turns up in the flow of an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the Latin name into SULIN; 'found' and 'of' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone the body needs to regulate blood sugar.

clue.text: The devil to come up to?

definitions.meaning: to come up to the required standard is to come up to the mark, the line drawn on the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Old Scratch is the devil's nickname, and come up to the line drawn for a race or boxing bout is the idiom.

clue.text: Attempt on 17 produces kaleidoscopic stuff

parts.note: a shot is an attempt
clue 17 is a Queen's Counsel, and a QC is known as a silk from the silk gown worn

explanation.surface: A barrister's try produces a dazzling array of material.
explanation.walkthrough: A QC is said to 'take silk' on appointment; 'on' and 'produces' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot fabric is woven with different-coloured threads so its colour shifts with the light, like a kaleidoscope.

clue.text: 1 out of 2 and the rest Spencer?

definitions.text: 1 out of 2 and the rest Spencer?

parts.note: one of two parts is a half
Marks and Spencer is the British department-store chain, so the word before 'and Spencer' is wanted

explanation.surface: A score of one from two, with a nod to a famous British shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Marks & Spencer is a well-known British high-street chain store. Scoring one out of two earns half the available marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting one point out of a possible two means receiving half of the available score in a test.

clue.text: Quality time included for the monarchy

indicators.note: one piece included in another sits inside it

parts.note: tone is a quality, as of sound or colour
HR, short for hour, is a unit of time

explanation.surface: Excellence and timing combine to suit the royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' only joins; the throne stands for royal power.
explanation.definitionFit: The throne stands by metonymy for the sovereign's power and office, the monarchy itself.

clue.text: New Labour -10: that can't be got over

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'New Labour -10: that can't be got over'; the wordplay needs N + an anagram of LABOUR + MINUTES, and the '-10' as held gives no MINUTES (10 here is REINS), so the clue looks garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: New Labour -10: that can't be got over

clue.text: Checks on dialysis?

definitions.meaning: ... check or restrain a horse, and to rein in is to curb
an old word for the kidneys, the organs dialysis stands in for

explanation.definitionFit: Reins are straps that restrain a horse, and in archaic English the word also meant the kidneys.

clue.text: Alien student coming in from Boston?

indicators.note: the student coming into the word means it is placed inside

parts.note: a stranger is an alien, an outsider
L, from the learner plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A foreign learner arrives from an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts L inside STRANGER. The Boston Strangler was the notorious 1960s serial killer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boston Strangler was the infamous murderer of thirteen women in 1960s Massachusetts.

clue.text: Fish is not well reported in the New Testament

parts.note: cod is a fish

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so these words give sounds rather than spelling

parts.note: is not well means is ill, run together when spoken

explanation.surface: A sickly fish turns up in a book of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid prints CODOCIL, but the wordplay builds the real word CODICIL. 'in the' is a joining phrase; the New Testament is a new addition to someone's will, not scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement to a will, so literally a later or new piece of one's testament.

clue.text: Honest fellow, Fred (not Harry)

parts.note: true means honest, faithful
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: An upright chap called Fred is distinguished from a president called Harry.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Trueman was a famous England fast bowler in cricket; Harry Truman, the US president, sounds the same but is spelt without the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Trueman was the celebrated Yorkshire and England fast bowler of the 1950s and 60s.

clue.text: Fellow taking another fellow's pigeon made poet feel like astronomer or conquistador

definitions.text: made poet feel like astronomer or conquistador

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
man's means belonging to another fellow
a homer is a homing pigeon

explanation.surface: A man borrows a friend's racing pigeon and is moved to verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats's sonnet 'On First Looking into Chapman's Homer' compares reading it to an astronomer finding a planet and Cortez seeing the Pacific; 'taking' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: George Chapman's translation of Homer inspired Keats to compare himself to a sky-watcher and to stout Cortez.

clue.text: Clear indeed, a pound maybe sought by 17

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: an act is a deed
quit can mean clear or free, as in quit of debt
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone is cleared and has a pound, perhaps, which a barrister hopes for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' must be split as 'in deed': in is the container signal and deed the outer piece. 'maybe' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A Queen's Counsel defending a client seeks a verdict of not guilty, a formal release from the charge.

clue.text: Crooked scoundrel hasn't died, but a very near thing

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order
the scoundrel not having the letter means it is removed

explanation.surface: A bent rogue escaped death, but only just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't' removes D from SCOUNDREL, leaving SCOUNREL, which 'Crooked' rearranges; 'but' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-run contest or escape is one decided by the narrowest of margins.

clue.text: Different sequel holds once sun's set on royal advice

indicators.note: one piece holding another contains it
different means changed, so the letters are put in another order
set as in set in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words once and sun, the possessive s adding no letter

explanation.surface: A new sequel comes along now the sun has set on royal guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different' rearranges SEQUEL to QUE..SEL, which 'holds' ENSCOUN, the rearrangement 'set' makes of ONCE SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Queen's Counsel is a senior barrister appointed to give legal advice in the monarch's name.

clue.text: Tyneside couple, monarchs of the system

parts.note: Tyneside is in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE
a couple is two
R for rex and K for king are two monarchs

explanation.surface: Two people from Newcastle rule over an organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area around Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A network is an interconnected system, such as of computers or railways.

clue.text: Red for offences that are pointless continuing

indicators.note: with no point, here the compass point East is removed

parts.note: crimes are offences
on means continuing, as in carry on

explanation.surface: Communist sympathies for misdeeds that keep going for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that are pointless' drops E, one of the compass points, from CRIMES; 'for' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep shade of red.

clue.text: Beastly housing left us with the needle

parts.note: a sty is housing for pigs, beasts

explanation.surface: A pig shelter left us holding a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is the needle that runs in a record's groove.

clue.text: Success in backing match for garments

definitions.note: plural because a twinset is a matching pair of garments

indicators.note: the success goes in, inside the other piece
backing means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a test is a match, as a cricket Test match
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A win in a reversed match leads to clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the match round to TSET before the success goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a woman's matching cardigan and jumper worn together, two pieces of clothing.

clue.text: Geographical feature formed by mountain in islands like this

indicators.note: the mountain goes in, inside the next piece

parts.note: thus means in this way, like this
M is an abbreviation for mountain

explanation.surface: A landform created by a mountain among islands looks like this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed by' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow strip of land joining two larger land masses, a geographical feature.

clue.text: The proverbial gun?

definitions.meaning: the proverbial, used as a noun, means a saying, a proverb
the ... was an early machine gun, named after Hiram ...

explanation.definitionFit: A maxim is a short general truth, and the Maxim gun was the first recoil-operated machine gun.

clue.text: Set fire to notes about soldier needing 17?

parts.note: lit means set fire to

indicators.note: notes around the soldier means the notes enclose him

parts.note: IOUs are promissory notes
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone burns IOUs around a soldier, who then needs a barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: A litigious person, always going to law, is forever in need of a QC.
explanation.definitionFit: Litigious means fond of lawsuits, so such a person keeps needing counsel.

clue.text: Dogfight participant?

parts.note: not an aerial combatant but someone who fights, and also a breed of dog

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is both a pugilist who fights in the ring and a breed of dog.

clue.text: See 6
Mayor's granny goes round tree with dog handler

parts.note: Ken Livingstone was then Mayor of London; the possessive s adds no letter

indicators.note: granny going round the tree means she surrounds it

parts.note: nan is a grandmother
the elm is a tree

explanation.surface: The mayor's grandmother circles a tree while walking the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was Mayor of London when the puzzle appeared; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A kennelman looks after dogs in a kennel, a handler of hounds.
